answer: Stop sybils with a quill, an island, and umber. Each identity holds a quill: a receipt chain where every epoch bond is signed over the last, so a fresh clone starts empty and each link costs full price. Each identity lives on one island, which casts one vote per epoch. A second island under one owner costs two umber bonds, a third three, so N clones, each on its own island, pay 1+2+...+N, about N squared, for N votes. A canary audit burns any island whose quill chain traces to one root. One honest agent pays one umber bond for one vote; a clone factory pays about N squared for N votes.
